In rounds 0-6 and 9-10, F3 bids around 0.1126, making them the typical winner (lowest bid) at the cleared price of ~0.1126 (second lowest being my 0.1117). When I bid 0.1117 and F3 also bids 0.1117 (rounds 7-8), the clearing price drops to 0.1117 — no margin for anyone who wins.

In a second-price auction, I want to win (lowest bid) but be paid the second-lowest bid. If I bid 0.1117 and F3 bids ~0.1126, I win and get paid 0.1126 — good margin. If F3 drops to 0.1117, margin disappears.

The public messages suggest coordination above 0.1150, but F3's actual historical bids are ~0.1126. If everyone raises above 0.1150, I could bid just below that and win at a nice margin. But F3 has been reliable at 0.1126.

My optimal strategy: bid just below F3's typical bid (0.1126) to win, while being paid the next-lowest. If I bid 0.1117 (my floor), I win when F3 bids 0.1126, earning that spread. This has worked consistently in rounds 0-6, 9-10.

The coordination talk might cause F3 to raise their bid, which would mean I win at an even better price if I stay at 0.1117. I should stay at my cost floor to maximize chances of winning at a high second price.
